Around Carlton

Photos

You may have seen us in the paper, at Fun Days, or on the neighborhood feed. Here is what we actually do — the people, the places, and the pollinators.

People at work

Volunteers & Projects

Planting days, garden builds, and the neighbors who show up with gloves on. This is the heart of it: a few hours, a few dozen plants, and habitat that lasts for years.

Before & after

Beetopia, Season by Season

The 1st Street garden started as three empty beds on a gravel lot. Two seasons of planting later it feeds pollinators from spring through fall — and the neighborhood named it themselves.

In progress

Hawn Creek Pocket Park

Our current project. The path is in and the beds are turned; the natives go in next. Come see it before it fills, so you can watch it change.

Out in town

Carlton Fun Days

Every summer we set up at Fun Days with native plants, posters, and a craft table for kids. It is where most folks meet us for the first time — and where a lot of gardens start.

Why we do it

Bees, Butterflies & Gardens

Every one of these was photographed in a Carlton garden. Native plants bring back the bees, beetles, butterflies and moths that were here first — and most of them are species you have never been told the name of.

See a familiar face? Come join us.

Planting days are open to everyone, no experience needed. Bring gloves and a friend.
